concept: A blue-hour environmental music portrait in a botanical research glasshouse: an original adult alto saxophonist sustains a phrase exactly as automated irrigation mist activates, lit by cool skylight and amber grow lamps in a natural 50 mm vertical mid-to-knee frame.
exact_prompt_en: Create a complex independent saxophone-semantics test photograph in a botanical research glasshouse at blue hour. An original adult saxophonist plays a sustained phrase while the automated misting system activates in blue skylight and amber grow light. Show an alto or tenor saxophone. The curved conical metal body ends in a flared bell beside her knee at realistic alto-saxophone scale. A single reed and ligature sit on the mouthpiece, with their tan cane and metal edges clearly visible. Dense keywork runs along the metal body, with linked rods, pads, key cups, and pearl touches remaining legible. The lips seal the reed mouthpiece while both hands operate keys, left on the upper stack and right on the lower stack. A cup mouthpiece and three piston valves do not substitute for the visible reed, ligature, curved conical body, and dense side keywork. Use Image 1 only as a scoped visible-appearance reference for this original adult performer: long dark center-parted wavy hair, softly defined eyes, muted rose lips, and a luminous natural skin-surface finish. A natural 50 mm f/4 vertical mid-to-knee frame contains her face, reed contact, both hands, keyed body, and bell; condensation and controlled reflections preserve humid depth.
negative_en: excessive HDR, impossible perspective, illustration look, low resolution, cartoon style, warped product geometry, broken window geometry, 3D render look, warped walls

composed.warning_boundary: Only advisory prompt-budget and uncovered-intent warnings remained; all three intents are bound literally. This PASS is preflight evidence, not pixel proof.

pixel_gate_results.summary: Thumbnail clearly reads as a curved, tapering, flared-bell alto saxophone.
Ligature hardware is clear, but a distinct tan cane single reed is not confidently separable at native scale; partial evidence is failure.
Linked rods, pads, cups, touches, guards, and levers remain legible at both scales.
Lips contact the mouthpiece region and both hands occupy plausible upper and lower key stacks.
The image lacks a cup mouthpiece and three-piston cluster and instead shows a reed-style crook, dense side keys, bowed body, and saxophone bell.

reference_scope_result.scope: visible adult facial appearance, hairstyle and hair color, makeup placement, and skin-surface finish only
reference_scope_result.summary: Long dark center-parted wavy hair, softly defined eye makeup, muted rose lips, and luminous natural skin finish remain visibly continuous while gaze and mouth position adapt to playing.
